review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the VeroneseRing, component, inclusion and zeroRingEquiv declarations in GradedRings/Veronese.lean. I checked Mathlib's GradedRingHom (RingTheory/GradedAlgebra/RingHom.lean) and the DirectSum map and congr API (Algebra/DirectSum/Basic.lean and Module.lean). I found no GradedRingEquiv in Mathlib, so selectedRingEquiv and selectedGradedHom do not duplicate an existing bundled concept. TailEquiv is a specific structure with no Mathlib counterpart. The one finding is that the hand-built inverse hom is a second copy of the inverse that DirectSum.congrAddEquiv already provides. This is a moderate case, because it overlaps with proof shortening. I also did not confirm that every use of selectedRingHomSymm (22 occurrences, all in this file) could be redirected without trouble. The competing-concept case is weaker than it would be for a standalone definition.

findings.problem: The file builds a separate inverse ring hom `selectedRingHomSymm` for `selectedRingHom`. To do this it adds `piece_mul_symm`, `pieceHomSymm`, `piece_one_symm` and two composition lemmas, about 55 lines in total. The inverse is built piecewise from `(pieceEquiv j).symm` into `DirectSum.of`. That is the same inverse Mathlib already packages for any family of component additive equivalences: `DirectSum.congrAddEquiv u` has `invFun := DirectSum.map fun i ↦ (u i).symm.toAddMonoidHom`. The result is two parallel versions of the inverse. One is `selectedRingHomSymm` with its own `_of` simp lemma. The other is `selectedRingEquiv.symm` with `selectedRingEquiv_symm_of`. `selectedGradedHomSymm` is also a separate hand-built declaration, not `.symm` of an equivalence.
findings.proposed_change: Define `selectedRingEquiv` directly from Mathlib's `DirectSum.congrAddEquiv (fun j => E.pieceEquiv n hNn j)`. Take `map_mul'` from the existing `selectedRingHom`; the two functions agree on `DirectSum.of` summands. A route through `RingEquiv.ofBijective` would also work. Then drop `pieceHomSymm`, `piece_one_symm`, `piece_mul_symm`, `selectedRingHomSymm` and the two `*_comp*` lemmas. Define `selectedGradedHomSymm` from `(E.selectedRingEquiv n hNn).symm`. Keep `selectedRingEquiv_symm_of` as the simp lemma, proved from `congrAddEquiv`/`DirectSum.map` on `of`. Keep `selectedRingEquiv` and the other names as the public API.
findings.benefit: This removes a second, parallel inverse construction and its simp and composition lemmas. The inverse is then `.symm` of one equivalence, which composes with Mathlib's RingEquiv API. The `piece_mul` fact would need to be proved once instead of in both directions.
